subject.title: Feature Request: Gateway lifecycle hooks (onSubagentComplete, onToolCallThreshold, onTurnComplete)

question: Should OpenClaw expose these lifecycle boundaries through HOOK.md workspace/internal hooks, through typed plugin hooks only, or through a split surface with different payload/permission levels?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the requested behavior changes public extension API, trusted local code execution, session-state visibility, and possibly config defaults; automation should not choose that contract shape.

options.title: Split safe workspace events from typed plugin control
options.body: Expose a minimal observation-only workspace event such as subagent:ended while keeping richer turn/tool lifecycle control in typed plugin hooks with documented permissions.

options.title: Typed plugin hooks only
options.body: Keep HOOK.md internal hooks for coarse operator automation and require lifecycle/memory/learning systems to use the plugin API.

options.title: Broader workspace lifecycle surface
options.body: Add all requested workspace events, including turn completion and tool-call thresholds, after maintainers define payloads, ordering, and config semantics.

recommendation.title: Split safe workspace events from typed plugin control
recommendation.body: Expose a minimal observation-only workspace event such as subagent:ended while keeping richer turn/tool lifecycle control in typed plugin hooks with documented permissions.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent hook docs and core subagent ownership work make this the best available routing owner for the product/security boundary decision.
